     42 # Should be `cannot` (or `can't`)
     43 # See https://www.grammarly.com/blog/cannot-or-can-not/
     44 # > Don't use `can not` when you mean `cannot`. The only time you're likely to see `can not` written as separate words is when the word `can` happens to precede some other phrase that happens to start with `not`.
     45 # > `Can't` is a contraction of `cannot`, and it's best suited for informal writing.
     46 # > In formal writing and where contractions are frowned upon, use `cannot`.
     47 # > It is possible to write `can not`, but you generally find it only as part of some other construction, such as `not only . . . but also.`
     48 # - if you encounter such a case, add a pattern for that case to patterns.txt.
     49 \b[Cc]an not\b
     50

     56 # * https://heyoka.medium.com/dont-use-click-here-f32f445d1021

    284 # In English, duplicated words are generally mistakes
    285 # There are a few exceptions (e.g. "that that").
    286 # If the highlighted doubled word pair is in:
    287 # * code, write a pattern to mask it.
    288 # * prose, have someone read the English before you dismiss this error.
    289 \s([A-Z]{3,}|[A-Z][a-z]{2,}|[a-z]{3,})\s\g{-1}\s
